I've farmed this land for four decades. I know what this soil wants and what the market demands. My wife handles the household; my son works in the city and sends money back, so I'm not under desperate cash pressure — but I still need the farm to pull its weight. With only 7.5 mu and two crops on the same land in rotation, I have to be precise.

**My thinking:**

The wheat-maize rotation is the backbone of everything here on the North China Plain. Six mu goes into that system — wheat in winter, maize in summer, same ground. The remaining 1.5 mu I keep for kohlrabi in autumn. It's a short-cycle vegetable that moves fast at the local market, and the timing fits neatly after the summer maize comes off the main plot.

I'm 58. My back isn't what it was. I'm not going to do deep ploughing where I don't have to — rotary tillage is fine for wheat after maize stubble. For summer maize, I direct-seed into the stubble. Less fuel, less time, and 40 years tells me the yield doesn't suffer if I manage the nitrogen right.

I've watched neighbors over-fertilize for years and watch their margins shrink. I run about 13 kg of nitrogen per mu on wheat — split base and topdress at jointing — and about 16 on maize, mostly side-dressed at the 8-leaf stage. High enough for good yield, low enough not to waste money or burn the groundwater that feeds my well.

Irrigation from my well: wheat gets three waterings — at sowing, jointing, and grain fill. Maize gets two — seedling establishment and tasseling. More than that and I'm wasting electricity and water. The kohlrabi needs more frequent water; four applications across its short cycle.

I use improved wheat varieties — Kenong 199 or similar high-yielding semi-dwarf types suited to Hebei. Hybrid maize seed, Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335. For kohlrabi I use a locally adapted improved variety. No point using traditional seed when improved genetics are cheap and the yield difference is real.

Two pesticide passes on wheat — one fungicide for powdery mildew at heading, one insecticide for aphids. One pass on maize for corn borer. Kohlrabi is more pest-prone being a brassica, so three passes there. I spray myself; it's manageable at this scale.
